newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Pou Chen down on Taiwan's China squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Pou Chen down on Taiwan's China squeeze.

text.p: Shares in Pou Chen Corp, the reported financier of a Taiwan-funded bank in Shanghai, fell sharply in late trade after the government said it would clamp down on unauthorised China investments, brokers said.
With 45 minutes left, Pou Chen had tumbled T$6.5 or 5.10 percent to T$121.
Taiwan's economics ministry on Wednesday urged local firms to stop unauthorised investments in communist rival China and vowed to ferret out and punish any illegal investments.
"We call for Taiwanese firms investing in China to stop investments as soon as possible before they gain approval," the economic ministry's Investment Commission said in a statement.
In early March, the commission warned local firms not to set up banks in China -- a day after a visiting mainland official confirmed that one Taiwan company already had done so.
Taiwan media have named Pou Chen owner Tsai Chi-chien and his brother Tsai Nan-feng as the financiers behind the planned Shanghai bank, First Sino Bank.
The Tsais have been unavailable for comment and executives of Pou Chen, a major investor in mainland footwear, refused to discuss the issue.
Taiwan has banned direct contact with China since a civil war split them in 1949.
